title: Brucie Drops 177.86, Randy Rides Caleb, and a Rookie Wins Her First Game: Week 1 Opens With a Bang
dek: No Banner only HULK posted a 79-point demolition to open the eight-team era, while The fumblers, Ghostu-Spider SZN and The Horse is Hea also started 1-0.
body: The eight-team era of the Buckaroo Football League is one week old, and Ramon is already its biggest problem. No Banner only HULK hung 177.86 points on Mekhi's Dawgs, a 79.5-point margin in a game the Dawgs were actually favored to win at 54%. Josh Allen threw in 35.66, Kenneth Walker III ran for 32.6, and D'Andre Swift added 31.9, three starters who each beat their projections by double digits. Brucie's title odds jumped from 11% to 47% in a single Sunday, which is the kind of number that makes seven other group chats go quiet at once.

The fun detail for the Chicago contingent: one of Ramon's best players this week was a Bears running back, working on behalf of the league's most famous Bills convert. Even the one blemish barely mattered. The Texans D/ST went for -4, and HULK still won by nearly 80. When your defense actively costs you points and you win by a full football score's worth of margins, it was your week.

Randy wasn't far behind. The fumblers flattened Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 146.16 to 75.96, powered by Caleb Williams going for 37.26 against a 16.39 projection and Derrick Henry piling up 34.8. Of course, Randy being Randy, he'll have something to grumble about: Colston Loveland posted a perfect zero at tight end. It's hard to complain about a 70-point win, but nobody in this league would bet against him finding a way. His title odds nearly doubled, from 15% to 28%.

The feel-good story of the week belongs to Zoe. In her first fantasy football game ever, Ghostu-Spider SZN beat Kaushal's Habibsters 129.56 to 108.6, a 21-point win as a slight underdog against the man with two Buckaroo Bowl rings. Zilgit even left David Montgomery's 27.4 points on her bench and still won comfortably, which suggests the rookie's ceiling might be higher than the scoreboard showed. Habib, meanwhile, watched his title odds crater from 17% to 3% and spent his first waiver run swapping the Browns D/ST for the Jaguars D/ST. It's a modest start for a two-time champ.

The tightest game of the week went to the commissioner. Sonny's The Horse is Hea edged Alan's Team Pillbert 106.42 to 102.1, winning as a 46% underdog despite Jahmyr Gibbs putting up 31.1 for Philly. Four points was the whole difference, and Sonny immediately went back to work, adding Mark Andrews and dropping T.J. Hockenson at tight end. Oddly, the win cost him in the projections: his title odds dipped from 9% to 4%, so the model is apparently unimpressed with how he got there.

Now for the bench blunders, and two of them belong to the losers. Jordan sat Ashton Jeanty, who went for 29.7, on his way to the week's lowest score; JMoney's playoff odds now sit at 3%. Mekhi had it worse in a way: Ja'Marr Chase started and gave him 2.2 points against a 16.44 projection, while Christian Watson scored 29.7 on the Dawgs' bench. Kai probably knows more football than anyone in the league, but this one was gone either way, since even that swap wouldn't have come close to Ramon's number. Mekhi's title odds fell from a league-best-tied 17% to 1%.

Week 2 serves up an immediate main event: the rookie against the juggernaut, as Ghostu-Spider SZN takes on No Banner only HULK. Zoe gets her first shot at the team everyone wants to see knocked down. Mekhi faces Randy in a game the Dawgs badly need, Jordan tries to get off the mat against Sonny, and Alan and Kaushal meet in a battle of 0-1 teams with something to prove. It's one week in a 14-week season, but somebody is starting 0-2, and it won't feel like a small thing.

bios.1: Sonny squeaked past Alan by 4.32 as an underdog and then retooled at tight end, adding Mark Andrews for T.J. Hockenson. The defending champ is 1-0, though the model dropped his title odds to 4%. Jordan's struggling squad is up next.
bios.2: Randy's squad rolled up 146.16 behind Caleb Williams' 37.26 and Derrick Henry's 34.8 to bury Jordan by 70. A zero from Colston Loveland is the lone smudge on a dominant debut. Title odds sit at 28%, second in the league.
bios.3: Jordan posted the week's lowest score, 75.96, while Ashton Jeanty's 29.7 sat on the bench in a 70-point loss to Randy. Playoff odds stand at just 3% after one week. JMoney gets the commissioner next and plenty of room to climb.
bios.4: Alan got 31.1 from Jahmyr Gibbs and still came up 4.32 short against Sonny as the slight favorite. Philly sits 0-1 with 32% playoff odds. Kaushal awaits in a battle of teams that expected better.
bios.5: Mekhi was favored and got run over by 79, with Ja'Marr Chase managing 2.2 and Christian Watson's 29.7 stuck on the bench. Title odds plunged from 17% to 1%. Randy's red-hot offense is next, and Kai needs a waiver-wire miracle quickly.
bios.6: Kaushal ran into a rookie on a heater and fell 129.56 to 108.6, watching his title odds tumble from 17% to 3%. A defense swap to the Jaguars was his first response. A Week 2 meeting with Alan is a chance to get the two-time champ back on track.
bios.7: Ramon opened the season with 177.86 points and a 79-point rout of the Dawgs, sending his title odds rocketing to 47%. Allen, Walker and Swift all went over 30, and the only thing that went wrong was a -4 from the defense. Next up: the rookie, with everyone in the league quietly rooting for her.
bios.8: Zoe won her first-ever fantasy game, beating two-time champ Kaushal 129.56 to 108.6 even with 27.4 points stranded on the bench. The rookie is 1-0 with 76% playoff odds. Her reward is a date with the league's hottest team in Week 2.
